name: infobroker

tools.name: infobroker_search_web
tools.description: Search the web, encyclopedia, academic, and code sources through one interface with automatic provider selection and a fallback chain. Use when you need broad or batched search, query autocomplete (suggest), query expansion (expand), ranked passages from the top pages (deep), or a multi-variant research compile that deep-reads each variant (research), and optional in-process analysis of the returned results (analyze: topics, entities, clusters, timeline). Do NOT use for a URL you already have (use infobroker_fetch_page), for high-stakes claim verification (use infobroker_verify_claims), for stored-report recall (use infobroker_manage_kb search), or for academic citations (use infobroker_get_citations). Caches results in the local knowledge base, enforces per-provider rate limits, and needs no API key for the free providers. `task_type` forces a dispatch chain (for example academic) when the automatic classification picks the wrong one. `fresh: false` keeps KB-first sufficiency, `fresh: true` skips KB recall and searches external providers, and `fresh: 'blend'` keeps cached KB results alongside fresh external results. `collection` scopes KB recall to a named collection. An array `query` is searched in parallel and merged, and a failed element is reported in `meta.per_query` without failing the batch. A measurable attribute (attendance, population, percentage, date) returns a sourced `facts` entry before prose, with `meta.fact_status`. Returns a JSON envelope prefixed `[OK]` or `[ERROR]` with status, provider, results, and meta.

anyOf.description: Multiple queries to search in parallel (max 5); a failed element is reported per input without failing the batch

query.description: Search query: a single string, or up to five strings searched in parallel

task_type.description: Force a dispatch chain by task type (auto-classified when omitted)

max_results.description: Number of results to return (1-30, default 8)

safe_search.description: Safe-search filtering: on, off, or strict (default on)

time_range.description: Restrict results to day, week, month, or year

priority.description: Route by intent: speed, quality, privacy, or free_only

suggest.description: Return query-autocomplete strings instead of results (default false)

expand.description: Return query-expansion strings instead of search results

deep.description: Read the top results and return each page's ranked passages against the query

research.description: Research compile: fan out to derived query variants and deep-read each, returning passages grouped by variant (default off)

analyze.description: Attach in-process analysis to the response: topic terms, entity mentions, semantic result clusters, and a dated timeline. Derived from the returned results only; adds no outbound request (default false)

fresh.description: Knowledge-base recall mode: false keeps KB-first sufficiency, true skips recall and searches external providers, blend keeps KB results alongside fresh external results (default false)

collection.description: Knowledge-base collection to recall from (scopes KB recall only; ignored when fresh is true)

content_type.description: Source kind to search: docs, issue, changelog, blog, spec, or all (default all)

language.description: Preferred result language (ISO 639-1, e.g. 'de'). Providers that cannot honor it report it in meta.ignored_params

tools.name: infobroker_fetch_page
tools.description: Fetch a URL and extract clean content via a renderer (Jina Reader by default; native-HTTP, Wikipedia, Internet Archive, arXiv, and Stack Exchange alternatives). Use when you have a URL and need readable text, passages ranked against a question, or the page's last-updated date. Do NOT use for topic search (use infobroker_search_web) or cross-source claim verification (use infobroker_verify_claims). `question` returns passages ranked against it, sized by `passage_size` and capped by `max_passages`; `crawl` bounds the same-origin crawl to config caps; `extract` adds JSON-LD, OpenGraph, and microdata; `renderer` selects the backend, and native_fetch is the keyless fallback when Jina is throttled or anti-bot challenged. `max_length` truncates the returned text only; a truncated page is written in full to a temp file. Makes external HTTP calls and needs no API key. A fresh knowledge-base copy is returned before an outbound fetch when available. Fetched pages auto-index into the knowledge base unless the content policy flags them (see infobroker_manage_kb): flag mode returns without storage, block mode refuses. Unreachable URLs return an [ERROR] envelope with remediation; when a DOI resolves, a blocked page falls back to Crossref metadata or an open-access copy, then to an Internet Archive snapshot, and reports `meta.fallback_kind`. Paywalls, access restrictions, and anti-bot blocks return `access_blocked`; connectivity failures return `network_error`; a non-http(s) URL returns `invalid_input` naming the read tool. Success returns an [OK] envelope with status, provider, results, and meta.

anyOf.description: Multiple URLs to fetch in parallel (max 5)

url.description: URL to fetch: a single URL, or up to five URLs fetched in parallel

renderer.description: Renderer: jina (default), native_fetch, wikipedia, internet_archive, arxiv, or stack_exchange

question.description: Question to extract ranked passages for, instead of returning the whole page

passage_size.description: Target words per passage (default from config)

max_passages.description: Number of passages to return (default from config)

detect_date.description: Detect and report the page's last-updated date (default from config)

crawl.description: Bounded same-origin crawl: recursively fetch same-origin pages up to config caps (default off)

extract.description: Return structured metadata (JSON-LD, OpenGraph, microdata) alongside the content (default off)

raw.description: Return the extracted page text directly instead of a JSON envelope (single URL; not with crawl or extract)

tools.name: infobroker_inspect_providers
tools.description: Inspect configured search providers: list their state, run a live health check, or report build and spec identity. Use when searches return empty or slow results and you want provider status, quota, or latency, or when choosing which backend to trust. Do NOT use to search (use infobroker_search_web) or to read a page (use infobroker_fetch_page). Read-only: it never modifies configuration, providers, or stored data. `list` snapshots provider state (including each provider's derived privacy posture) and `status` filters it; `health` runs a live outbound probe against `provider` (required for the `health` action; subject to that provider's rate limits, so it can be slow; for a `generic_http` provider with no `health_endpoint` the probe is a real search query and may consume provider quota or credits); `spec` reports build and spec identity plus local state health (config drift, backend capabilities, update status) and session counters. Returns an [OK] or [ERROR] JSON envelope with status, provider, and results.

tools.name: infobroker_verify_claims
tools.description: Verify one or more contested claims against independent sources and return confidence-scored findings. Use when a claim is high-stakes or contested and you need agreement, contradiction, and gaps surfaced with confidence scores, or when a finished draft needs a claim-by-claim fact-check in one call. Do NOT use for simple lookups or broad search (use infobroker_search_web) or citation formatting (use infobroker_get_citations). The loop recalls prior findings from the knowledge base, then searches providers and writes findings back; `max_iterations` bounds the refinement passes and per-provider rate limits apply, with one HTTP-call budget shared across a batch. Supply exactly one of `query` (one claim, or a string the server splits into up to five) or `claims` (a list of independent claims seeded verbatim); a batch returns one finding per distinct claim in caller order, identical claims are collapsed and report every input index they cover, and a claim with no attributed source is reported unverified rather than dropped. `priority` routes the pool by intent (speed, quality, privacy, free_only); `providers` restricts the pool and omitting it uses the full dispatch chain; `confidence_threshold` sets the bar for confirmation, and findings below it are reported unverified. Each source carries a `span` locating its supporting sentence and an advisory `modality` (asserted, reported, speculative) that never changes confidence. Returns an [OK] or [ERROR] envelope listing confirmed, contested, and unverified findings with per-source claims, spans, and confidence scores.

query.description: One claim to verify; the server splits it into up to five sub-claims. Supply either query or claims, not both

claims.description: Independent claims to verify as a batch (bounded by corroboration.max_batch_claims, default 10); seeded verbatim and returned one finding per distinct claim in this order, with identical claims collapsed and every input index reported. Supply either query or claims, not both

confidence_threshold.description: Minimum confidence to report a finding as confirmed (0-1, default 0.8)

providers.description: Optional array of provider slugs to limit the search to

priority.description: Route the corroboration pool by intent

tools.name: infobroker_manage_kb
tools.description: Manage the local knowledge base: search cached content, ingest text or URLs, list/get/delete entries, view stats, read persisted claim records, and manage at-rest encryption. Use when you need to archive a generated report (ingest with source_type 'report' and save_to 'kb'), revisit stored content, or manage encryption keys. Do NOT use for fresh external search (use infobroker_search_web) or to fetch a new page (use infobroker_fetch_page). The delete action is destructive and cannot be undone; a lost encryption key makes the store unrecoverable by design. Parameter semantics: `action` selects the operation; `query` for search, `text`/`url` plus `title` and `collection` for ingest, `source_url` for get/delete, and `operation` with `key_file` for the encryption sub-actions; `source_type` and `freshness_tier` tag an ingest and filter search/list; `save_to` defaults to 'kb', `format` to 'markdown', `max_results` to 8; `last_updated` is auto-detected from fetched URLs when omitted; `receipt` attaches a claim-to-source manifest to a report ingest and `verify_report` rechecks it offline. Responses carry an [OK] or [ERROR] envelope: search/list/get return entries, stats returns counts, delete reports the chunks removed.

key_file.description: Path to a key file (generate_key writes here and refuses an existing path; rekey reads the target key from here). Never pass the secret itself — only a file path.

query.description: Search query (search action) or claim-text filter (claims action)

text.description: Raw text to index (for ingest action)

url.description: URL to fetch and index (for ingest action)

source_type.description: Source type (tag on ingest; filter on search/list)

last_updated.description: Source last-updated date to store (e.g. '2026-08-24'); auto-detected from fetched URLs when omitted

save_to.description: Where to save (ingest action): kb, disk, or both. Default kb

source_url.description: Source URL filter (get/delete/claims action), the report identity for verify_report, or identity for ingest

max_results.description: Maximum results to return (search/claims action; 1-50, default 8)

receipt.description: Optional verification receipt for a report ingest (REQ-110): claims with cited sources, report-level Source Register URLs, and optional report metadata (REQ-114). The server computes the report hash, per-source hashes, and the digest; any caller hashes or digest are ignored. Requires source_type 'report' and KB storage.

verdict.description: Fact-check verdict for this claim (for example True, Mostly True, Half True, Mostly False, False, Misleading, Unverifiable)

likelihood.description: Calibrated likelihood term (for example almost certain, likely, even chance, unlikely)

sources.description: Report-level Source Register URLs, linked to the stored report (REQ-110)

report.description: Optional report-level manifest metadata (REQ-114), stored with the receipt

shape.description: Workflow shape that produced the report

assumptions.description: Key assumptions stated separately from evidence

tools.name: infobroker_reload_config
tools.description: Re-read the configuration file and apply provider, rate-limit, and knowledge-base changes without restarting; active connections are preserved. Use when you have edited config.json or config.local.json, or when passing `patch` to change configuration programmatically. Do NOT use to inspect configuration or provider state (use infobroker_inspect_providers). `patch` deep-merges a partial config into the user layer (config.local.json), rejecting unknown top-level keys, backing up the previous layer, and validating the merged result before writing; `migrate` true backs up and applies registered user-layer migrations before reloading. The call re-reads the startup configuration source and reports any user-layer schema drift. If the new configuration is invalid, the previous configuration stays active and an error is returned. Returns an [OK] or [ERROR] JSON envelope.

patch.description: Partial configuration deep-merged into the user layer (config.local.json) before reloading; unknown top-level keys are rejected and the previous layer is backed up

migrate.description: Back up and apply registered user-configuration-layer migrations before reloading (default false)

tools.name: infobroker_get_citations
tools.description: Return academic references for a query as BibTeX citations with title, authors, year, venue, DOI, and URL. Use when scholarly writing needs a reference list. Do NOT use for general web search (use infobroker_search_web) or contested-claim verification (use infobroker_verify_claims). `query` is a natural-language topic; `max_results` sets the reference count, and larger values take longer and span more sources. References are gathered from every enabled academic provider, deduplicated by DOI (title when absent), and each provider's status is reported in `meta.providers`; a zero-result answer names the providers tried. Needs no API key when at least one scholarly source is reachable; if every source fails it returns an [ERROR] envelope with remediation, and queries respect per-provider rate limits. Returns an [OK] or [ERROR] JSON envelope.
